# Additions to Daniel Chapter 2 (Susanna) — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus (Theodotion recension), Additions to Daniel 2
**Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADD_002_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Decision

Susanna is a detective story with a sustained narrative arc and a climactic trial scene. Three demands are in tension: (1) the story must move — pacing matters; (2) the depiction of the elders' desire and coercion must be honest without being gratuitous; (3) the wordplay at the climax (mastic/split, oak/hew) is built into the text and cannot be omitted. PNEUMA provides the narrative voice; LOGOS provides the legal and formal precision; EMET preserves nuances at key theological moments. The tree-pun is retained in all versions with bracketed notation.

---

**1** There was a man living in Babylon whose name was Joiakim.

**2** He had married a woman named Susanna, daughter of Hilkiah — beautiful in appearance and God-fearing.

**3** Her parents were righteous and had raised their daughter according to the law of Moses.

**4** Joiakim was very wealthy and had a garden adjoining his house; the Jews used to gather there because he was the most respected of them all.

**5** In that year two elders were appointed from the people to serve as judges — the very kind the Lord had in mind when he said: "Lawlessness came out from Babylon, from elders who were judges, who only appeared to govern the people."

**6** These men frequented the house of Joiakim, and all who had legal disputes came to them.

**7** At midday, when the people withdrew, Susanna would go in and walk in her husband's garden.

**8** The two elders saw her every day going in and walking about, and they became consumed with desire for her.

**9** They let their minds become corrupted and averted their eyes from heaven, forgetting their duty to render just judgments.

**10** Both of them were tormented with passion for her, yet neither one disclosed his grief to the other,

**11** for each was ashamed to confess his desire — his longing to lie with her.

**12** Day after day they watched for an opportunity to see her.

**13** One day they said to each other, "Let us go home — it is the dinner hour." They departed and each went his own way —

**14** only to turn back and meet at the same spot. Pressing each other for an explanation, both admitted their desire; and from that point they began watching together, looking for a time when they could find her alone.

**15** One day, while they were waiting for the right moment, she came in as usual with only two maidservants, and wished to bathe in the garden, for the day was hot.

**16** No one else was there — only the two elders, hidden and watching.

**17** She said to her maidservants: "Bring me soap and oil, and shut the garden doors so that I can bathe."

**18** They did as she instructed: they shut the garden doors and went out by the side entrances to fetch what she had requested; they did not see the elders, because they were hidden.

**19** The moment the maidservants were gone, the two elders sprang up and rushed toward her, saying:

**20** "The garden doors are shut and no one can see us. We desire you — consent to us and lie with us.

**21** If you refuse, we will testify against you that a young man was here with you, and that is why you sent your maidservants away."

**22** Susanna groaned and said: "I am trapped on every side. If I do this, it means death for me; if I refuse, I will not escape your hands.

**23** Yet it is better for me to fall into your hands without doing it than to sin in the sight of the Lord."

**24** And Susanna cried out with a loud voice; and the two elders also cried out against her.

**25** One of them ran and threw open the garden doors.

**26** When the household servants heard the commotion in the garden, they rushed in through the side entrances to see what had happened to her.

**27** When the elders told their story, the servants were mortified, for nothing of this kind had ever been said about Susanna.

**28** The following day, when the people assembled at the house of her husband Joiakim, the two elders arrived filled with their wicked scheme to have Susanna put to death.

**29** They said before the assembly: "Send for Susanna, daughter of Hilkiah, the wife of Joiakim." And they sent for her.

**30** She came with her father and mother, her children, and all her relatives.

**31** Now Susanna was very graceful and beautiful.

**32** The wicked men ordered her unveiled — for she was veiled — so that they might feast their eyes on her beauty.

**33** Those with her and all who knew her were weeping.

**34** The two elders stood up before the assembly and laid their hands on her head.

**35** She wept and looked up toward heaven, for her heart trusted in the Lord.

**36** The elders said: "We were walking alone in the garden when this woman came in with two maidservants. She shut the garden doors and dismissed the maidservants.

**37** Then a young man who had been hiding came to her and lay with her.

**38** We were in a corner of the garden; when we saw this wicked deed, we ran toward them.

**39** We saw them together, but the man we could not hold, for he was stronger than us; he threw the doors open and fled.

**40** But we seized this woman and demanded to know who the young man was.

**41** She refused to tell us. This is our testimony."

**42** The assembly believed them, since they were elders of the people and judges; and they condemned her to death.

**43** Then Susanna cried out with a loud voice and said: "O eternal God, who know what is hidden and know all things before they come to pass —

**44** you know that they have given false testimony against me. And now I am to die, having done none of the things these men have wickedly invented against me."

**45** And the Lord heard her voice.

**46** As she was being led away to death, God stirred up the holy spirit of a young man named Daniel,

**47** and he cried out with a loud voice: "I am innocent of this woman's blood!"

**48** All the people turned to him and said: "What are you saying?"

**49** Standing in their midst, he said: "Are you really so foolish, O sons of Israel? You have condemned a daughter of Israel without examination, without establishing the truth clearly.

**50** Return to the court — these men have given false testimony against her."

**51** All the people turned back in haste. And the elders said to him: "Come, sit among us and tell us what you know, since God has given you the standing of an elder."

**52** Daniel said to them: "Separate them from each other. I will examine them."

**53** When they had been separated, he called the first elder and said to him: "You who have grown old in wickedness — now the sins of your former years have caught up with you:

**54** you have rendered unjust judgments, condemning the innocent and releasing the guilty, though the Lord said, 'The innocent and the righteous you shall not put to death.'

**55** Now tell me: if you truly saw her, under what tree did you see them together?" He answered, "Under a mastic tree [schinos]." Daniel said: "That lie has condemned you, for the angel of God has already received the sentence from God and will split you in two [schizein]."

**56** Setting him aside, he called the other and said to him: "You, offspring of Canaan and not of Judah — beauty has seduced you and lust has corrupted your heart.

**57** This is how you treated the daughters of Israel, and they lay with you out of fear; but a daughter of Judah would not endure your lawlessness.

**58** Now answer me: under what tree did you catch them together?" He answered, "Under a holm oak [prinos]." Daniel said to him: "Your lie has condemned you too, for the angel of God waits with his sword to hew you in two [priein], and so destroy you both."

**59** Then the whole assembly cried out with a great voice and blessed God, who saves those who hope in him.

**60** They rose up against the two elders, for out of their own mouths Daniel had convicted them of false testimony.

**61** They did to them as they had wickedly plotted to do to their neighbor; acting in accordance with the law of Moses, they put them to death. And innocent blood was saved that day.

**62** Hilkiah and his wife gave praise to God for their daughter Susanna, together with her husband Joiakim and all her relatives, because no shameful thing had been found in her.

**63** From that day forward Daniel was held in great esteem among the people.

**64** And King Astyages was gathered to his fathers, and Cyrus the Persian received the kingdom.
